summary.intent: Implement a 'layered publish' feature for the release executor: add deferred confirmation (issue and settle) seams so package publishes, notably npm, are no longer confirmed serially. Verify it with simulator tests, a real Verdaccio end-to-end test and updated docs, then ship it as a PR stacked on #320.
summary.outcome: Added deferral seams to the provider traits, capability and registry provider, and rewrote the executor loop with issue/settle. Extended the simulator and added tests, added a two-package real-Verdaccio npm test, updated the spec, ADR 3, architecture doc and operator guide, and added a changeset. `just ci` passed (exit=0), then the work was committed, pushed and opened as a PR stacked on #320.

repo: Release code lives in crates/callisto-graph/src/commands/release/ (capability.rs, provider/mod.rs, provider/registry.rs) and release_execution.rs holds the executor loop.
The release subsystem has a simulator with world, intent, scenarios and invariants, plus enumeration tests. Any change to executor semantics must be mirrored in the simulator's entry points.
Real-registry (Verdaccio) tests are gated to Linux only, so they do not run on macOS unless the gate is temporarily lifted.
Spec criteria live in docs/specs/release.json (execution order and rerun criteria are affected by deferral). Docs touched alongside code: ADR 3, docs/architecture/release.md, docs/releasing.md.
Changes require a changeset, and `just ci` is the full pipeline that catches end-to-end tests assuming serial npm confirmation.
Work is organized as a stack of PRs on worktrees under .claude/worktrees/.

code.finding: The executor loop was rewritten to separate issuing a publish from settling its confirmation, enabling layered/deferred confirmation instead of serial confirmation.
The registry provider gained deferral seams so confirmation can be settled later, which matters for late-registry visibility cases.

workflow: Batch edits were done via throwaway Python scripts in /tmp, which made multi-file edits repeatable but needed follow-up fix scripts when anchors or paths were wrong.
When new tests failed, the traces were read first to decide whether the test or the executor was wrong. Here the simulator tests were corrected.
The Linux-only test gate was temporarily lifted to prove the npm path locally with a throwaway Verdaccio install, then restored and checked with a change listing.
Running the whole suite and the full CI pipeline before shipping caught assumptions in existing tests.

friction: Two of the new simulator tests failed initially, including the late-registry trace, and needed several correction rounds (fix_layered_tests, 2, 3).
A duplicate function and a wrong path in the first executor rewrite needed a fix script before it compiled.
The real-registry test target ran no tests locally because of the Linux-only gate, so it had to be temporarily changed to run on macOS.
Documentation spec anchor text had to be fixed before the doc edits applied.
Assertion text changed after formatting, so it had to be located again before editing.
open_items: Real-Verdaccio tests remain Linux-gated, so the macOS local run was only a temporary verification; CI on Linux is the authoritative check.
The PR is stacked on #320 and depends on it landing first.
